issues.issue: The rationale treats absence of contrary tradition as enough for this label but does not distinguish the explicit expectation that opponents would deny the tomb if they could. A probabilistic argument from expected but absent evidence is not automatically the catalogue definition of treating true merely because not disproved. Reconsider whether the actual inference, its qualifications and positive lines cross the material definition threshold.

The rationale needs to distinguish citing the reported survey author about the scope of the claimed consensus from treating scholarly status as deciding tomb historicity. The frozen claim/inference concern evidential status and sample scope; an unverified report alone does not establish fallacious authority reliance. Reconsider the precise conclusion and materiality.
